LESSON: IMITATIVE SPEAKING: PRONUNCIATION

Grade: Grade 7
Subject: ARABIC
Strand: Listening and Speaking
Topic 1.2: Imitative Speaking: Pronunciation

SECTION 1: WELCOME

Hello! This is a study lesson on Imitative Speaking: Pronunciation. Read the explanation, follow every worked example, then do the practice. This is original CBC Learn content written from KICD outcomes — not a copy of a commercial textbook.

Big question: where do your parents work?

SECTION 2: WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

By the end of this lesson, you will be able to:

1. identify family members by their names and professions
2. apply appropriate intonation and stress in pronouncing words for fluency
3. appreciate the role of immediate family members for social co- existence

SECTION 3: STUDY NOTES (READ AND LEARN)

WHAT YOU ARE STUDYING: IMITATIVE SPEAKING: PRONUNCIATION
Subject: ARABIC · Grade: Grade 7
This is a learner study lesson (not a teacher guide). Read every part, follow the models, then practise.

BIG PICTURE
Imitative Speaking: Pronunciation helps you succeed in ARABIC. You will understand it, practise it, and use it at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

KEY FACTS: IMITATIVE SPEAKING: PRONUNCIATION
Language skills grow by daily practice: listen carefully, speak clearly, read every day, write neatly.
Model → guided practice → independent practice.
Always use complete sentences when writing answers.

PART 1: Identify family members by their names and professions

What this means
In this part you learn to identify family members by their names and professions. You will use ideas from at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: identify family members by their names and professions.
2. Listen, speak, read, then write using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Model reading: Read a short paragraph about “Imitative Speaking: Pronunciation”, then retell it in 3 sentences.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can identify family members by their names and professions. Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 2: Apply appropriate intonation and stress in pronouncing words for fluency

What this means
In this part you learn to apply appropriate intonation and stress in pronouncing words for fluency. You will use ideas from at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: apply appropriate intonation and stress in pronouncing words for fluency.
2. Listen, speak, read, then write using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Model speaking: Say 4 clear sentences about Imitative Speaking: Pronunciation to a partner.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can apply appropriate intonation and stress in pronouncing words for fluency. Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 3: Appreciate the role of immediate family members for social co- existence

What this means
In this part you learn to appreciate the role of immediate family members for social co- existence. You will use ideas from at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: appreciate the role of immediate family members for social co- existence.
2. Listen, speak, read, then write using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Model writing: Write 5 neat sentences using new words from this lesson.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can appreciate the role of immediate family members for social co- existence. Write or say your answer clearly.

PUT IT TOGETHER
Close your notes and say aloud: what Imitative Speaking: Pronunciation is, one example, and one way you will practise this week.

SECTION 4: QUICK EXAMPLES

Example 1: Read a short paragraph about “Imitative Speaking: Pronunciation”, then retell it in 3 sentences. (skill: identify family members by their names and professions)

Example 2: Say 4 clear sentences about Imitative Speaking: Pronunciation to a partner. (skill: apply appropriate intonation and stress in pronouncing words for fluency)

Example 3: Write 5 neat sentences using new words from this lesson. (skill: appreciate the role of immediate family members for social co- existence)

SECTION 5: PRACTICE NOW

1. Write 5 sentences (or show 5 clear steps) that teach Imitative Speaking: Pronunciation to a classmate.
2. Practise this skill: identify family members by their names and professions.
3. Practise this skill: apply appropriate intonation and stress in pronouncing words for fluency.
4. Practise this skill: appreciate the role of immediate family members for social co- existence.
5. Make one local Kenya example of Imitative Speaking: Pronunciation from your county, market, farm, or school.
6. Mark your own work: What did you get right? What will you redo?

SECTION 6: WORK TO DO (HOME / REVISION)

1. In your exercise book, make a one-page revision sheet for Imitative Speaking: Pronunciation: meaning, 3 examples, 5 practice items.
2. Teach a parent/guardian or younger sibling one part of this lesson (2 minutes).
3. Answer in writing: Why should a Grade 7 learner study Imitative Speaking: Pronunciation?
4. Prepare for the quiz: cover the Remember box and recite it.

SECTION: THINK ABOUT IT

1. where do your parents work?
2. Why is it good to pronounce words correctly?

SECTION: REMEMBER

1. Know what Imitative Speaking: Pronunciation means in your own words.
2. Use local Kenyan examples, not only definitions.
3. Practise in small steps, then check your work.
4. Be able to: identify family members by their names and professions.
5. Be able to: apply appropriate intonation and stress in pronouncing words for fluency.

Now complete the Revision Quiz. Open Answers only after you finish.

— CBC Learn · Original study notes from KICD outcomes (Strategy 2)
